notes: The MPCW-6 is a wireless/wired scoring console controller for driving Nevco scoreboards (baseball, basketball, football, etc.) -- not a conventional video/audio-signal device, so none of its ports are HDMI/SDI/etc. Physical I/O details came from the "MPCW Product Spec" PDF linked from the manufacturer product page (a generic spec sheet covering the whole wired/wireless MPCW line, not an MPCW-6-specific document; the product page itself left the dimensions field blank). Confirmed from that spec diagram: one external DC power-adapter input, two "control cable outputs" for wired operation, and two receptacles for an optional coiled-cord hand-held remote time switch (works from either receptacle). Exact connector part numbers/pin counts are not published -- the control-cable and handset jacks appear in the diagram as small round modular jacks with coiled telephone-style cords, so "rj45" was used as the closest available connector id in the taxonomy rather than a confirmed spec (no bandwidth grade applies; these are not Ethernet ports). The console also has a recessed power toggle switch and a physical "MPCW system key" (a keyed lock on a tether) for owner authentication -- neither is an electrical signal/power connector, so both were omitted from the port list. A separate companion "MPCW Receiver" box (its own power adapter, RF antenna, and "output jacks to scoreboards") is required to bridge the wireless signal to a scoreboard; that accessory's I/O was not included here since it is a distinct product from the MPCW-6 console itself. Unit is a tabletop console (11" x 9.5" x 4.125", ~3.75 lb), not rack-mountable, so rackUnits was omitted.

ports.name: Power Adapter Input
ports.note: External wall-wart DC power adapter plugs into the console; exact barrel size not published in the spec sheet.

ports.name: Control Cable Output 1
ports.note: One of two 'control cable outputs' used for wired scoreboard operation (can run simultaneously with wireless). Spec diagram shows a small round modular jack with a coiled cord, not a true Ethernet port -- rj45 is the closest taxonomy match, not a confirmed connector part number.

ports.name: Control Cable Output 2
ports.note: Second of two wired control-cable outputs; same connector-type caveat as Control Cable Output 1.

ports.name: Hand-Held Switch Receptacle 1
ports.note: Receptacle for the optional coiled-cord hand-held remote time switch ('will operate from either receptacle'). Modular phone-jack-style connector approximated as rj45; not a network port.

ports.name: Hand-Held Switch Receptacle 2
ports.note: Second receptacle for the hand-held remote switch; same connector-type caveat.
